Pink, orange, and green chart lines and Material teal / red confidence cards. The default.
An Okabe-Ito-derived palette designed to stay distinguishable under deuteranopia, protanopia, and tritanopia. Confidence cards use sky blue, neutral, and amber instead of teal, neutral, and red.

Magenta, yellow, and cyan chart lines — like highlighter pens on the page. Visibly different from Rainbow at a glance; the light theme uses deeper variants for readability. Safe under red-green color blindness.
Drag the handles to reorder how these sections appear on the home screen.
The confidence chip and the per-model chart pull from these models. Picking more gives a richer spread; fewer means a tighter focus. At least two stay selected.
Pick the regional forecaster automatically — UKMO in the British Isles, JMA in Japan, GFS + GEM in North America, etc. Turn off to choose models yourself.
You\'ve picked %1$d models — the most the chart stays readable for. Deselect one to add a different model.
European — generally the most accurate global model. 0.25° open feed, out to 15 days.
German (DWD) — strong in Europe and at short range. Native hourly.
American (NOAA) — strong over North America. Native hourly.
Canadian (ECCC) — strong over North America. 3-hourly on the open feed.
French (Météo-France) — strong over France and Western Europe. Native hourly.
British (UK Met Office) — historically second only to ECMWF. 3-hourly on the open feed.
Japanese — strong over Asia-Pacific. 3- to 6-hourly on the open feed.
ECMWF\'s AI model — skillful out to 15 days, so it carries the second-week charts. Some detail charts may not show a line for it.
